Responses containing go/be auxiliaries, a negative particle, or two stems are excluded.

These Pothwari paj- broken/infinitive responses match the former stem with the regional voiceless outcome of initial voiced aspiration; the j is retained. This is a bhajj- family analysis, leaving the original loss of aspiration/tone realization at the survey’s recorded level, and it does not cover the SSNP y-spelled forms awaiting font checks.

The whole affirmative response is analysed synchronically as sleep + go in that order, with ordinary imperative vowels and western s-to-h outcomes preserved. The compound segmentation is an analysis of these survey expressions, not a claim that Turner prints each expression; no additional tense auxiliary or negative is omitted.

Both lexical components are represented in their surface order, retaining h for s and ordinary finite ending variation. This is a modern compound-verb analysis from the whole response; forms with ambiguous standalone -ga, an extra particle, or a second elicited answer are excluded.

These whole imperatives are bhāg + jā “run away”, with yāti as the go auxiliary; the ordered components distinguish this g-stem from the bhajj- branch. The segmentation is inferred from the complete modern expression, without adding a claim about its regional borrowing route.

The whole imperative is the g-retaining bhāg run stem from Turner’s bhagna branch plus le “take” from the lāti family, used as a light verb. Both components are included in order; the source ɛ vowel is retained and the link does not treat the full predicate as one inherited stem.

The full past expression has bhāg run (Turner bhagna branch) followed by gāyo gone (gata), with the linking vowel retained. Both lexical pieces are represented as ordered components; the analysis does not confuse the go auxiliary with part of the inherited run stem.
